$comment: A RECORD of hosted-database verification that was actually performed, so
deploy:check can reflect proven reality without contacting the hosted
project itself (it never does, by design).
This is a claim with a date and a method, not a live check. deploy:check
says so when it reads this file. If the hosted schema changes, this record
becomes wrong and must be re-verified — that is the cost of recording a
Dev Update 6.0 found this file describing three applied migrations while the
hosted project had twenty-four. The record was stale, not the database. It is
now reconciled against the hosted migration history rather than re-applying
anything: production was already correct, and the documentation was not.
Never put keys, row contents, or user data in this file.

migrationsApplied.verifiedBy: schema query: last_active_at column and activate_birth_profile function present
migrationsApplied.rehearsed: twice against a scratch database built to the hosted schema

migrationsApplied.verifiedBy: schema query: ask_conversations and ask_messages present, RLS enabled, 8 policies
migrationsApplied.rehearsed: twice against a scratch database built to the hosted schema

migrationsApplied.method: Supabase management API apply_migration; migration history reconciled to the exact repository version with the Supabase CLI
migrationsApplied.verifiedBy: exactly one migration-history row; public schema usage and SELECT available to service_role for all 16 user-owned tables
migrationsApplied.destructiveStatements: none; GRANT USAGE and GRANT SELECT only
migrationsApplied.rollback: commented REVOKE statements are included in the migration
migrationsApplied.preflight: 16 table row counts, storage counts, client grants, policies, and RLS settings recorded before application

rlsVerification.method: scripts/rls-check.js against the hosted project with two live disposable users
coverage: cross-user read, update, delete, and activate all denied
ownership cannot be forged on insert
cross-user Ask Orbit conversation access denied
anonymous callers receive no rows and cannot write
rlsVerification.note: This hosted run predates every table listed in notCovered. scripts/rls-check.js was extended in Dev Update 6.0 to cover all of them and passes 38/38 against the LOCAL stack; it has not been re-run against hosted. Policies for those tables exist in the applied migrations, but existing is not holding.
rlsVerification.cleanup: disposable users deleted; hosted row counts returned to pre-test values

dataIntegrity.note: All 16 user-owned table row counts and storage bucket/object counts matched before and after the grant-only migration. Client grants, policies, and RLS-state digests were identical.

serviceRoleVerification.importantContext: The hosted platform had already granted service_role all ordinary table privileges on these tables before this migration. This migration added only the explicitly reviewed USAGE and SELECT grants; application code confines service-role construction to the production account-deletion path.

migrationHistoryReconciliation.method: Supabase management API list_migrations, compared name by name against supabase/migrations/
migrationHistoryReconciliation.note: Timestamps in the hosted history differ from the repository filenames for migrations applied through the management API, which restamps them. They were matched by name, not by version.

unrecordedInHostedHistory.finding: Absent from the hosted migration history.
unrecordedInHostedHistory.evidence: information_schema.role_table_grants shows authenticated and anon already hold ordinary table privileges on the public tables this migration grants; Supabase grants these by default and RLS is what restricts access.
unrecordedInHostedHistory.action: None. Re-applying a grant that is already in place would be noise. Recorded so the gap is known rather than rediscovered.

pendingApplication.status: NOT APPLIED to hosted. Verified against the local stack only.
pendingApplication.blocks: First-party analytics, the beta metrics panel, and every measurement this update adds. The application degrades quietly without it — beacons fail and are swallowed by design — so nothing breaks, and nothing is counted either.
pendingApplication.action: Owner decision, as every hosted migration is. See docs/environment-safety.md.

securityAdvisors.method: Supabase management API advisors, security category, against the hosted project
securityAdvisors.note: Clean at the time of checking. Must be re-run after the analytics migration is applied to hosted, because that is when new tables and a security-definer function reach the project.

authenticationSettings.reason: GoTrue's configuration lives in the service environment, not in a queryable table, so it cannot be read from SQL or the management API used here. It is deliberately NOT inferred from how many accounts have a confirmation timestamp, which would be a guess dressed as a fact.
authenticationSettings.action: Owner: read Authentication → Sign In / Providers → Email → 'Confirm email' in the Supabase dashboard and record the answer here.
